message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (numbers 0‑9 + two of each action card). 4 Wild and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | | **Setup** | Shuffle, deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1️⃣ Draw one card if you can’t play.
2️⃣ Play one card that matches either color, number, or symbol.
3️⃣ If you have no playable card, you may play a Wild or Wild Draw Four (subject to rules). | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Winning a Turn** | When you play your last card, shout “Uno!” If you forget, the next player can call you out and you must draw two cards. | | **Scoring** | After a round ends, players add up the point values of the cards left in their opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Game End** | First to reach the agreed‑upon score wins. | **Key Tips** * Keep track of what’s been played to anticipate opponents’ moves. * Use Wild Draw Four strategically—if you’re caught playing it illegally, you’ll have to draw 4 instead of 2. * Remember to say “Uno” before your opponent takes their turn; otherwise you’ll get penalized. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak house rules (e.g., “draw two on a wild” or “no wild draw four unless you have no other options”) to suit your group. Happy playing!
